proxy_overhead_direct.definition: Per model call, the guest-local time from sending the model.request frame to receiving the first model event, minus the emulator-local time from that call's arrival to its first byte.
proxy_overhead_direct.limiter: inferred, not traced: the controller's share before the upstream call is under 5 ms at p50 in every arm; the E2B arms' extra 10 ms at p50 over the local runner is the frames' transit through E2B's command stream

perf.control_limiter: database calls are 99 to 100 percent of the control window, 17 queries at p50; PGlite SELECT 1 is 0.47 ms at p50 on this host

rss_pglite.note: the heap grows about 0.5 MiB per run throughout; the earlier heap-snapshot comparison placed it in PGlite's in-process wire messages

rss_postgres.database: a disposable PostgreSQL 17 container on the build machine, reached from the host through an SSH reverse tunnel; one migrated database per arm, created and dropped by the bench; none was left after the run
rss_postgres.result: no durable growth: after 18 warmup runs the heap stays between 181.6 and 183.5 MiB, and RSS settles at 456 to 460 MiB
rss_postgres.latency_caveat: SELECT 1 through the tunnel is 26.7 ms at p50, so this run's control and warm-run times measure the tunnel, not a production database

defects_found_in_final_pass: Harness: lane i asserted completion with message_user only; it now calls an MCP tool served by the controller and checks its result reached the model.
Harness: no lane drove the S6 home-move fence live; lane home-move-fence starts a run during a real move's copy.
Harness: the bench's local arm failed setup in the live bundle, since S8's LocalWorkerProvider copies the repository's skills/agent, which the bundle does not carry. It now passes the bundled copy.
defects_found_live_and_fixed_s5: The worker template from #229 did not build: E2B runs build steps as the sandbox user, which cannot create /workspace or write /opt. The makeDir and the bundle copy now run as root.

Every worker create from #229 was refused with 400 'Timeout cannot be greater than 1 hours': the provider asked for the 4 hour TTL. It now asks for the lower of the TTL and maxTimeoutMs, 1 hour by default.

E2BVolumeFiles from #241 could not reach any volume: this self-hosted deployment does not serve E2B's volume content API (every call 404), and the SDK sends those calls to api.<domain> unless E2B_VOLUME_API_URL is set. It now works through a sandbox that mounts the volume. Its default owner 1000:1000 was also wrong: the sandbox user is 1001.
Review: WORKER_TTL_SECONDS said 4 hours while the provider capped the sandbox at 1. The TTL is now 1 hour, and a cap below it logs a warning.
Review: volume-file writes were not atomic. They now go through a temporary file renamed over the target, which replaces a link instead of following it and never lands inside a directory.

Review and live: a volume-file sandbox E2B killed stayed cached. Lane h found that E2B reports it as a TimeoutError mapped from envd's 502, not SandboxNotFoundError; both now evict and replace it once, after destroying the old one.

Review: close stopped at the first failed destroy, and the migration command's report could be replaced by that error. close now waits for every destroy, and the command reports a failed close on its own.
Review: /workspace was root-owned 0755 while the guest runs as uid 1001. The template hands it to the sandbox user; lane i checks the guest can write there.

Review round 2: a 502 from envd triggered a sandbox replacement, but a live sandbox behind a failing proxy answers it too, and its delayed rename could publish the retry's partial upload. Replacement now needs proof of death (SandboxNotFoundError, the SDK's 'killed or reached its end of life' TimeoutError, or a 502 with the control plane no longer listing the sandbox); each attempt stages under a new name; a dead sandbox whose destroy failed is destroyed again at close.

Review round 2: the staged file was uploaded at 0644 and chmodded after. It is now created 0600 by the guest user and the upload writes into it; lane h checked live that the upload keeps mode and inode.
Review round 2: a staged file whose placement could not start stayed on the volume. It is removed with its own 30 s deadline, also on cancellation.

Review round 3: SandboxNotFoundError and the 'killed or reached its end of life' TimeoutError can both come from a live sandbox behind a failing proxy. Every death signal now needs the control plane to no longer list the sandbox before it is replaced.

After #243 merged: lane c's fixed port 47001 was drawn by a worker's rpc.statd from the ephemeral range, which accepted the probe and never answered, so the lane hung. Its listeners now use ports below that range and each probe gives up after 3 s.
After #243 merged: the template's Pi layer installed ripgrep for a grep tool that is the guest's own JavaScript walker. The layer now installs nothing, and the rebuilt template has no rg.

#243's relay mask parsed every string and key of a relayed transcript as JSON, and each failed parse threw: 28 to 36 ms per call for 30 to 34 KB transcripts on the host, by a timing probe in the relay that was not committed. It now parses only text that opens an object, an array or a string, and prepares the secrets once per walk; masking is unchanged.
found_live_not_fixed: runtime-worker-routing.test.ts 'rolls back a takeover requeue whose attempt outcome cannot be written and counts the crash' (from #243) fails in most runs of that file alone, with Prisma's 'No record was found for an update', on this branch's code before and after the mask fix. It passes alone and in the full suite.
